summary: PR 1682 at 6d5477605b06c845b25f9260c59599dc33a0aedd correctly reserves EAGLE/NEXTN target-verify slots in scheduler generation clipping. This is a verified partial source-level fix, not proof that the reported H800 TP8 CUDA illegal-memory-access incident is fully resolved.

tests.what_was_measured: The pre-existing base suite passed 8 tests and 542 subtests; it did not cover speculative reserve slots.
Base selected 52 new tokens for input length 262091, so adding four verify slots reaches 262147 and exceeds context length 262144.
Candidate suite passed 9 tests and 542 subtests, including the new four-slot context-boundary regression.
Reported boundary and six independent cases passed, followed by 3,895 exhaustive combinations of small contexts and reserve widths.
Candidate Python source and regression test compiled successfully.
Imported scheduler from /job/repo/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py using Python 3.12.3 and Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2; visible accelerator was AMD Instinct MI355X gfx950.

remaining_counterexamples: A CUDA Graph/static-buffer or dangling-pointer failure independent of scheduler token clipping would remain unfixed by this Python-only change.
Any request path that bypasses Scheduler.init_req_max_new_tokens would not receive this new reserve.
The exact Qwen3.5-397B hybrid Mamba/attention, FA3, TP8, overlap-scheduled H800 failure may have an additional or different cause.
remaining_limitations: The assigned hardware was one AMD MI355X gfx950 GPU, not eight NVIDIA H800 GPUs.
CUDA, FA3 CUDA kernels, TP8, CUDA Graph replay, NVIDIA Xid 31, and the production illegal-memory-access failure could not be reproduced.
No native source changed in the candidate, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
The deterministic tiny Llama serving fixture cannot qualify the affected Qwen3.5 hybrid architecture or distributed CUDA failure and was therefore not used as proof.
